item.title: Dodgers boost pitching depth by signing ex-Cardinals prospect
item.description: Rich Storry-USA TODAY Sports. Dodgers boost pitching depth by signing ex-Cardinals prospect appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Dodgers added pitching depth by signing right-hander Tink Hence to a minor league contract, giving a former top 100 prospect a fresh start. The 24-year-old spent his professional career in the St. Louis Cardinals organization. He reached Triple-A with Memphis, and the deal gives Los Angeles another pitcher with upper minors experience. St. Louis selected Hence with the 63rd overall pick in the 2020 MLB Draft. He signed out of Watson Chapel High School in Pine Bluff, Arkansas, after committing to the University of Arkansas. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Athletic’s Katie Woo shared news of the deal Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, crediting MiLB Central’s Chase Ford with first reporting the signing. “The Dodgers signed RHP Tink Hence to a minor-league deal, as @_chaseford reported. Hence, 24, was a second-round pick in 2020 by St. Louis and a former top 100 prospect who ultimately didn’t pan out in their system.” Hence put together his best season in the upper minors with Double-A Springfield in 2024. He went 4-3 with a 2.71 ERA and struck out 109 batters in 79 2/3 innings. A rib cage injury interrupted his 2025 season, when he pitched just 21 1/3 innings. In 2026, he went 1-3 with a 6.64 ERA in 20 1/3 innings for Memphis. The Cardinals designated Hence for assignment on August 1 and sent him outright to their Florida Complex League affiliate five days later. He became a minor league free agent in November. Across 94 career minor league appearances, including 71 starts, Hence posted a 3.50 ERA and struck out 347 batters in 277 2/3 total innings tossed. He has yet to make his major league debut. That experience gives the Dodgers another option for their minor league rotations heading into 2027. The contract adds depth without requiring a spot on the major league roster. Los Angeles had yet to announce where Hence would begin his first season with the organization. item.title: Wizards Are Showing Flashes of an Exciting Offense Despite Struggles
item.description: The Washington Wizards haven’t had the start to the season they hoped for, but offensive performances have given fans something to be excited about. Despite a recent eight-game losing streak, Washington has shown that they can put up points. Through 16 games, the Wizards are 5-11 and are averaging 110.8 points per game . Washington still has plenty of time to improve and gel, but their recent performances show that this team can become exciting to watch when everything comes together. Washington’s Offense Shows Promise One of the more positive things about the Wizards lately has been their ability to score. Washington scored 132 points in their second game against the Atlanta Hawks . The next game, the Wizards put up 140 points in a double overtime loss against the Detroit Pistons . Three Wizards players scored at least 30 points against Detroit, something Washington hasn’t done since 1969 . TRAE TO SEND US TO OVERTIME pic.twitter.com/0hlGd3CqiX — Washington Wizards (@WashWizards) November 13, 2026 Washington followed that performance by scoring 119 against the Houston Rockets and then 120 against the Memphis Grizzlies the next night. Even though they lost eight games in a row, Washington still showed they have several players who can step up offensively. Washington has shown how dangerous their offense can be when they get the ball moving. Against Detroit, the Wizards finished with 33 assists, meaning players were giving each other opportunities to get involved instead of relying on one main scorer. If Washington can continue sharing the ball and getting contributions throughout the lineup, its offense can become much harder for opponents to handle. Consistency Is Key for the Wizards While the Wizards have put together some impressive offensive performances, they still haven’t been able to do it consistently. Washington scored 75 points against the Oklahoma City Thunde r on Nov. 7, which is a big difference from some of their other recent performances. In their recent win, the Raptors held them to 103 points. But the past few games have shown what Washington is capable of. Scoring at least 110 points in three straight games is a positive sign, especially considering how much the team has been struggling to regain their original team chemistry. The bigger issue they face is keeping that level of play going for all four quarters. For instance, Washington had a 10-point halftime lead when they played Memphis after shooting 56% from the field. Once the second half started, things quickly changed as the Grizzlies outscored the Wizards 42-18 in the third quarter and took control of the game . It’s becoming frustrating how quickly a strong performance can slip away. Washington has shown it can build leads and score quickly, but those stretches don’t mean much if the team can’t keep it going. item.description: Benny Sieu-USA TODAY Sports Blazers’ Damian Lillard gets completely real on returning to Milwaukee to play Bucks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Portland Trail Blazers will be facing the Milwaukee Bucks , which makes it the first time that Damian Lillard gets to play against his former team . Lillard spent two seasons with the Bucks, and though he may not have had the success he wanted, it’s still good to return somewhere he created memories. “It’s good to be back,” Lillard said. “Met some good people here, had some good experiences here, so when you’re anywhere for a year or two, you have those types of relationships that you form, and you get used to being around people for that amount of time on a daily; it’s good to step back into that space and see those faces. I’m happy to see some people that I’ve come across along the way.” Damian Lillard on finally playing against his old #Bucks team and understanding why he was waived: pic.twitter.com/n3Q4q1sgZj — Lance Allan (@lanceallan) November 19, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lillard tore his Achilles in the playoffs with the Bucks and was then waived and stretched that offseason, which led him to return to the Blazers. There’s no question that Lillard has always been a hard worker, and going through that situation wasn’t going to change how he approached work. “Being waived and then having to fight my way back to being able to get back in form and play at a good level again, it was tough,” Lillard said. “But it was something I was up for, and it’s no other way I would’ve gone out. I wasn’t going to fold to a significant injury or a tough time. This was the only way for me. To do the work and put the time in and make sure I was able to get back and finish my career how I want.” Now, Lillard is back at full health, and the Blazers are playing some good basketball as they’re currently 9-5 and sixth in the Western Conference. item.title: South Carolina coach Shane Beamer names best team in college football
item.description: South Carolina Gamecocks coach Shane Beamer previewed their tough home game against the Georgia Bulldogs . Beamer has been on the hot seat this season and could save his job with a win over No. 1 Georgia . No. 21 South Carolina is fresh off an ugly 34-6 road loss to the Arkansas Razorbacks . Beamer dodged questions about injuries and did not answer if South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers would be able to play against Georgia. Sellers did not appear on the SEC availability report. “Got a big challenge this week," Beamer said. "No. 1 team in the nation coming in here. That is real. You watch the tape. They are absolutely the best team in the nation. "They are firing on all cylinders. Offense, defense, special teams. Kirby (Smart) has done a fabulous job. Again, they are talented. They are well coached. They are disciplined. I think they’re the least penalized team in the conference. They play hard. They play physical. You’re going to have to beat them in order to win the football game. They’re not going to beat themselves. So much respect for their program. "I’ve told you guys before, whenever we’ve played Georgia, the time that I spent knowing Kirby for a long time, at the time that I spent coaching for him, made me a better coach and ton of respect for how they do things. And we’ve got a big challenge on Saturday night. Having said that, we got an awesome opportunity on Saturday night too." On Georgia's rushing attack "This is a different offense rolling in here Saturday night (compared to Arkansas last week) with the way that they can run it, throw it, how explosive they are," Beamer said. "I mean, they got tight ends that can take the ball and run eighty yards for a touchdown or catch it eighty yards for a touchdown. They got receivers that can do it. They got running backs that can do it. I mean they’re really humming right now, certainly. So for us it’s, you know, doing our job playing with great physicality great effort and, and got to tackle well talked about that this morning and executing." On renewing the rivalry with Georgia "I know what this game means to this game and next week means to the fans," Beamer said . "It’s odd that we haven’t played these guys since 2023. So it’s great to have them back on the schedule. "And I remember thinking when the schedule came out, looking at it like, man, we got Georgia and Clemson back-to-back, to finish the season. But as a competitor, that’s what you want, certainly. On the bright side, I picked the UW game correctly and nearly nailed the score. Let’s hope for a better outcome this week. Indiana @ Washington (+7.5) The Huskies return home after a successful road trip in a week where 7/9 Big 10 home teams are underdogs. Of course, the Dawgs have not lit the world on fire at home this year, losing to Minnesota, Iowa, and Penn St at Husky Stadium (naming rights deal be damned, I will continue to say Husky Stadium). Indiana is the defending National Champions but has not looked as dominant as they did a year ago. In fact, they changed QBs to Grant Wilson last week against USC and the 6th year Old Dominion transfer looked rock solid. In fact, that game was a bounce-back of sorts for Indiana, who struggled to beat Michigan and Minnesota in the two previous games. Regardless of who plays QB, the RB duo of Beebe and Richard has kept the offense moving all season. The Husky defense has forced opponents to drive the length of the field and avoid making mistakes. It has worked for most of the season and led to lots of forced turnovers. Indiana has been disciplined and physical enough to avoid those mistakes, so it could be a tough game for the defense to make big plays. And that’s the side of the ball where the Huskies have more often had the advantage this year. They stymie teams who run the ball much better than the Huskies, so it is likely to be another one-dimensional attack. item.title: Lions, Bucs injury report: QB Baker Mayfield returns to practice, feels ‘ready’ to play
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers looks to pass in the third quarter of the game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (7-2) and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) were back on the practice field Thursday, and with the Lions holding a walkthrough Wednesday, this was our first real look at where Detroit’s players stand with injuries. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . N o practice C Cade Mays (low ankle sprain) Earlier in the week, coach Dan Campbell said he didn’t think Mays would reach a point where he could play this week. With an estimated “no practice” on Wednesday and an official “no practice” on Thursday, it’s probably too late for a player who’s been injured for multiple weeks to return to practice and play in a game with only a few days remaining. Mays is almost certainly out for this Sunday. Limited practice RB Sione Vaki (ankle) DL Tyler Lacy (shoulder) LB Joe Bachie (knee) CB D.J. Reed (hip) — won’t rush back, unlikely to play vs. Bucs CB Khalil Dorsey (ankle) CB Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) Vaki has been nursing his ankle injury for nearly two weeks, but he hasn’t missed any game time and practiced this week, suggesting he could play again on Sunday. Lacy’s best asset is his ability to stop the run, and with the Bucs grinding out yards on the ground, he’d give the Lions a big boost if he is available to play on Sunday—which sounds realistic based on how coaches have been discussing him this week. Bachie has been solid special teams depth since being called up to the active roster, but little is known about his injury. If he can’t play, the Lions have five other linebackers on the active roster and Owen Pappoe (elevated for special teams last week) on the practice squad. Reed is getting some work on the practice field this week, but he is taking his recovery process slowly after rushing back too soon last year. item.title: Gladbach courting Leverkusen's Andrich and Lazio defender Doekhi
item.description: Gladbach courting Leverkusen's Andrich and Lazio defender Doekhi Borussia Mönchengladbach are keen to explore the transfer market in January. If possible, any targets should boast Bundesliga experience. Two names have been linked with the Rhineland club this evening in the form of Robert Andrich and Danilho Doekhi. According to Sky Germany's sources, Gladbach have already inquired about the Bayer Leverkusen player and ex-Union Berlin star. It remains to be seen whether the duo will be available. Andrich, for his part, is dissatisfied with his playing time at Leverkusen. The 32-year-old could possibly imagine a change of scenery and move to Leverkusen's rivals in the hope of increased playing time. Doekhi, on the other hand, moved from 1.FC Union Berlin to Serie A outfit Lazio on a free transfer in the summer. item.title: Rams’ Puka Nacua Issued 3-Game Suspension Amid IL Stint
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The NFL issued a three-game suspension to Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. View this post on Instagram A post shared by LA Sports Report (@lasportsreport) What Did Puka Nacua Do? Nacua received the punishment following reports of him making an antisemitic remark and biting a woman on Dec. 31, 2025. His accuser filed a lawsuit March 25 for assault and battery against Nacua, though his attorney denied he said anything antisemitic and called the biting incident as “horseplay.” The wide receiver also got in trouble with the league last season, drawing criticisms league-wide for making an antisemitic gesture and publicly making negative comments about NFL officials on a livestrea with Adin Ross. “When I appeared the other day on a social media livestream, it was suggested to me to perform a specific movement as part of my next touchdown celebration,” Nacua wrote via Instagram. “At the time, I had no idea this act was antisemitic in nature and perpetuated harmful stereotypes against Jewish people. I deeply apologize to anyone who was offended by my actions as I do not stand for any form of racism, bigotry or hate of another group of people.” While Nacua did receive the suspension, it comes at a fortuitous time for the Rams. Nacua is currently has a minimum of three games remaining on his injured reserve stint, meaning the Rams won’t lose the wideout for any additional time after his return from injury. Oct 25, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) warms up before the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images What is Puka Nacua’s Injury? Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains in the final snap of the Rams’ win against the Commanders in Week 9, and also received a turf toe diagnosis. He also dealt with some other injuries early in the season, such as a minor calf strain and a nagging groin injury. Head coach Sean McVay is yet to provide a timetable for his return, but the Rams will hope it’s sooner rather than later. Nacua leads the team with 70 receptions and 715 receiving yards this season, and had his best game of the year prior to his injury. He caught 14 passes for 150 yards and scored a touchdown, marking the third time in as many weeks he had done so. Having dodged Nacua’s suspension, the Rams will look to continue their four-game win streak and insert themselves into the playoff picture with a strong finish to the season. item.title: Rory McIlroy’s Sports Psychologist Reveals Why He Has Become a Better Golfer
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ajayi Segun Rory McIlroy’s longtime sports psychologist, Dr. Bob Rotella, has revealed how the Northern Irishman has improved his approach to golf, particularly when it comes to accepting missed putts. GOLF.com shared comments from McIlroy and Rotella about the influence the psychologist has had on the four-time major winner’s game. McIlroy explained how their conversations help him stay focused during tournaments and how Rotella has a way of making things simple. Rotella has also noticed a change in McIlroy’s approach, believing he now understands that there are different ways to play good golf without depending on perfect shots throughout a round. ALSO READ: Brooks Koepka Admits Missing Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup Frustrates Him McIlroy Explains How Rotella Helps His Game McIlroy explained that Rotella does a good job of breaking things down into smaller points that he can remember and use during competition. He also values the way the psychologist relates golf to other parts of life, helping him maintain perspective when the pressure increases. The Northern Irishman admitted that it is easy to get caught up in the outcome of tournaments, especially when he wants to win. However, Rotella has helped him concentrate on the things he can control rather than worrying too much about the final result. McIlroy explained that he does not always go to the psychologist looking for new advice. item.description: Upgrades to the Rock Creek Tennis Center plan to touch nearly every aspect of the site. Gensler The Rock Creek Tennis Center in Washington, D.C., has a $25 million funding plan behind it to help the site not only better host community tennis, but remain as the long-term home of the DC Open. Rollingwood Sports—supported by the Washington Tennis and Recreation Revitalization Coalition—also announced a new 60-year lease with the site’s owners, the U.S. Department of the Interior. The modernization of the historic facility aims to create a public, urban tennis facility that addresses long-deferred capital and maintenance at the center while improving every element of the public site that has hosted the DC Open since Arthur Ashe, Donald Dell and John Harris founded it in 1969. “As tennis continues to grow at an extraordinary pace nationwide investing in quality courts and facilities is essential to sustaining that momentum,” says Craig Tiley, CEO of the U.S. Tennis Association. “This project represents a groundbreaking and transformational opportunity to meet growing demand in the Washington, D.C., region, delivering world-class facilities that will serve professional, collegiate and high school players, as well as the broader community.” Every tennis court at the Rock Creek Tennis Center will get rebuilt from the ground up. Gensler The initial phase of improvements includes rebuilding all the tennis courts from the ground up, upgrading court lighting, sandblasting, painting and making repairs to rusted and deteriorated stadium locations, renovating public restrooms, updating food and beverage facilities, support spaces and locker room (while making them available to the public) and upgrading other critical building systems. Plans also call for a college and high school competition and training facility on site. Already, Howard and Georgetown universities have expressed excitement over the updates. Following next year’s Mubadala DC Open, the indoor tennis bubble will get replaced. Along with the physical improvements, Rollingwood and the coalition plan an expansion of programming for all levels. “Our goal is to make the Rock Creek Tennis Center one of the very best public urban tennis and recreation facilities in America and deliver something extraordinary for the district and our region,” says Mark Ein, chairman of Rollingwood Sports. “We are going to make the investments that his historic facility has needed for decades, create more opportunities for people to play tennis and other sports year-round and ensure one of the world’s great professional tennis tournaments stays in Washington, D.C.” The Rock Creek Tennis Center is home to the DC Open. item.title: ‘Makes you a couple percent better’: 49ers pre Mexico City practice location may prove useful
item.description: Sep 14, 2025; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Detailed view of the San Francisco 49ers helmets against the New Orleans Saints during the first half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The San Francisco 49ers are set to spend Week 11 in Mexico City as they will face off against the Minnesota Vikings for their second international game of the year. But head coach Kyle Shanahan and the organization may have a few travel tricks up their sleeve that could give the 49ers an advantage. In Week 1, the 49ers faced the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, but the two teams took different travel approaches, benefiting one more than the other. The Niners headed to Melbourne a full week before the game, while the Rams showed up roughly 24 hours before kickoff. After the game, San Francisco’s decision to acclimate to a new environment before play proved to be effective, as they defeated the Rams 27-7. With their second international stint approaching, new challenges await, but the 8-1 Niners are already prepared. Mexico City creates a unique challenge for NFL teams because it sits at an elevation of about 7,350 feet, roughly 2,000 feet higher than the Denver Broncos’ home stadium. In preparation, the Niners have decided to spend the bulk of their practice week in Colorado Springs at the Air Force Academy’s Falcon Stadium, which sits at 6,621 feet. In a press conference on Nov. 13, Shanahan shared his perspective on altitude training and why he believes it helps the team in the long run. “I think it helps,” Shanahan said . “I grew up mainly in Denver, and I always know how bad it would be for me. It didn’t matter how good a shape you’re in. Like, when I came home from college, you’d run up the stairs and be out of breath. It takes some time to get used to it. It just is what it is with altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver, it’s always a challenge, and I know Mexico City’s higher than Denver. It’s not make or break by any means, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better.” Back in 2022, the team used the same tactic ahead of their game against the Arizona Cardinals in Mexico City; in the end, the 49ers defeated the Cardinals 38-10, proving acclimation may be advantageous. It will be interesting to see how play unfolds when two powerhouses collide, as the Vikings are 7-2 and tied with the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears for the NFC North lead. item.description: Kentucky Basketball has officially signed Ryan Hampton and Cherif Millogo during the NCAA fall signing period, the school announced on Thursday. Hampton is a 6-foot-6 wing from Dallas (TX) and is entering his senior season at Rockwell-Heath High School. He is a consensus 4-star prospect who was rated as high as the No. 6 overall recruit in the class of 2027 by Rivals at the time of his verbal commitment to the Wildcats. “We’re really excited for Ryan to join our program,” head coach Mark Pope said in a press release. “He brings great experience at a young age and has tremendous family pedigree. He’s an elite-level player in transition and can really get downhill. We love what he can bring to us off the bounce and as a cutter. On top of that, he has a great personality and will be a perfect fit with our culture.” Hampton began his high school career at Rockwell-Heath before playing at several prep schools including DME Academy, South Central Prep and Dynamic Prep. He opted to return to Rockwell-Heath for his upcoming senior season of high school basketball. Playing on the EYBL circuit this past summer for both LivOn and Nightrydas, Hampton averaged 18.5 points, 6.0 rebounds and 1.2 assists across 22 games. He scored 20 or more points in nine contests, including multiple outings with 29 points in the first session of 2026 Nike EYBL in Atlanta. Hampton was named to the Naismith High School Boys Player of the Year Watchlist in 2025 and has participated in multiple USA Basketball minicamps, including one in Indianapolis this past April. Hampton’s older brother, R.J., was a first-round draft pick in the 2020 NBA draft by the Milwaukee Bucks and spent four seasons in the NBA. His father, Rod, played college basketball at SMU and professionally in Asia and Europe. Millogo, a 7-foot-3 center originally from Burkina Faso in West Africa, is a consensus top-15 recruit and projects to be among the tallest players in Kentucky Basketball history. “Cherif brings a unique build and skillset to college basketball,” Pope said in a press release. “He has an amazing combination of size, mobility, and skill that are unmatched at this level. He can shoot from outside and is a fantastic finisher at the rim. We can’t wait to get him to Lexington and get to work.” Millogo began his high school career at Cambridge Arts, Technology and Science in Massachusetts before transferring to St. Francis (California) before his junior year. As a high school junior, Millogo averaged 24.7 points, 11.4 rebounds, 5.1 blocks and 3.8 assists per game, helping lead St. Francis to a 21-9 record. With the way receivers Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington are playing, it would be tough to see many targets anyhow. And shutdown he has been. The Jaguars’ secondary has had its share of struggles this season, but Hunter has been exceptional and is only getting better. Among Jaguars’ cornerbacks, Hunter is by far the least targeted. On average, he’s targeted once every 8.5 coverage snaps, compared to the 5.6, 6.5, and 4.7 snaps per target of Montaric Brown, Jourdan Lewis, and Jarrian Jones. When he is targeted, few are better. Hunter’s passer rating allowed of just 56.5 ranks eighth among NFL cornerbacks. Against the Titans, Hunter nabbed his third interceptions this season, flashing those impressive receiver skills of his. He may not be playing much receiver, but that doesn’t mean his ball skills aren’t regularly on display. He’s been particularly dominant in man coverage. He ranks first among all cornerbacks with a 0.0 passer rating allowed. On the season, Hunter has allowed just three of his 10 targets to be caught for 24 yards and two interceptions in man coverage. An even crazier stat, Hunter has yet to allow a touchdown in his NFL career. He’s only allowed two receptions of 20+ yards as well, according to Pro Football Focus. He isn’t targeted often, and when he is, he’s more likely to make a big play than he is to allow one. Bill Barnwell of ESPN recently listed Travis Hunter as his midseason All-Pro selection at cornerback. It’s important to remember, Hunter has yet to play a full NFL season, yet is already getting All-Pro consideration at a position he truthfully didn’t play all too much of as a rookie. The ceiling is the roof for Travis Hunter. It’s seemingly limitless.
